steps.note: Water over a bar = min(tallest wall on its left, tallest on its right) − its height. Two pointers start at the ends; each remembers the tallest wall it has passed.
Left side is the bottleneck (max 0 ≤ 0). Bar 0 (0) is a new tallest left wall — it holds no water.
Left side is the bottleneck (max 1 ≤ 0). Bar 1 (1) is a new tallest left wall — it holds no water.
Right side is the bottleneck (max 1 < 1). Bar 11 (1) is a new tallest right wall — it holds no water.
Left side is the bottleneck (max 1 ≤ 1), so the right wall is tall enough. Bar 2 holds 1 − 0 = 1. Total 1.
Left side is the bottleneck (max 2 ≤ 1). Bar 3 (2) is a new tallest left wall — it holds no water.
Right side is the bottleneck (max 2 < 2). Bar 10 (2) is a new tallest right wall — it holds no water.
Left side is the bottleneck (max 2 ≤ 2), so the right wall is tall enough. Bar 4 holds 2 − 1 = 1. Total 2.
Left side is the bottleneck (max 2 ≤ 2), so the right wall is tall enough. Bar 5 holds 2 − 0 = 2. Total 4.
Left side is the bottleneck (max 2 ≤ 2), so the right wall is tall enough. Bar 6 holds 2 − 1 = 1. Total 5.
Left side is the bottleneck (max 3 ≤ 2). Bar 7 (3) is a new tallest left wall — it holds no water.
Right side is the bottleneck (max 2 < 3), so the left wall is tall enough. Bar 9 holds 2 − 1 = 1. Total 6.
Right side is the bottleneck (max 2 < 3). Bar 8 (2) is a new tallest right wall — it holds no water.
Trapped water: 6 units (per bar: ['0', '0', '1', '0', '1', '2', '1', '0', '0', '1', '0', '0']). One pass, two pointers, two running maxima — O(n) time and O(1) extra space.
